subject: PivotalPay — Immediate headroom ceiling breach & reserved throughput shortfall
messages:
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: ops@pivotalpay.com, cto@pivotalpay.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: PivotalPay — Immediate headroom ceiling breach & reserved throughput shortfall

Hi Meera / PivotalPay team,

Thanks for the ping — I’m escalating this immediately. We’re seeing two correlated symptoms in your Dedicated pool: 1) sustained headroom depletion (pool at ~98% GPU utilization across the reserved nodes) and 2) reserved throughput falling ~30% below your committed baseline (affecting long-tail latency and an increased 5xx rate).

Initial ask: can we schedule an immediate 30-minute bridge (exec + ops) in the next hour? We want to:
- share current metrics and logs
- agree on a short-term mitigation (burst / model fallback / routing change)
- confirm remediation timeline and communications to your ops teams and downstream partners

I’ve looped in Marcus (SRE), Karthik (inference optimizations) and Priyom (customer success) to coordinate. I’m attaching a short CSV with the SLO delta and a draft mutual action plan.

We recognize this is high-severity; we’ll prioritize the pool and propose options that minimize customer impact.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Director, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

Attachments: pivotalpay-slo-metrics-20271102.csv, pivotalpay-mutual-action-plan-20271102.docx

Subject: Re: PivotalPay — Immediate headroom ceiling breach & reserved throughput shortfall

Lauren — thanks for the quick response. We’re in the middle of a high-volume promotional window; traffic spiked ~4x over the last 90 minutes which coincided with several vendor jobs hitting the same model route. Latency on critical endpoints climbed from 120ms p50 to ~1.3s p50; error rate (502/503) rose to ~4.7%. We’ve opened customer-facing runbooks and are seeing failed payments on ~0.4% of requests.

We need a mitigation that avoids a customer-impacting rollback. We’re available for a bridge at 09:40 PST.

— Meera Singh
PivotalPay, Head of Payments Ops
ops@pivotalpay.com

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 09:12 AM lauren_bishop@redwood.com wrote:
> Hi Meera / PivotalPay team,
> 
> Thanks for the ping — I’m escalating this immediately.

Short RCA notes before the bridge:
- Observation: Dedicated GPU pool nodes (rp-pivotal-01..04) show per-GPU utilization spiking 97–100% starting 07:50 PST.
- Token throughput (aggregate): typical 1.8M tokens/min -> peaked 7.6M tokens/min over a 30m window.
- Reserved throughput metric drift: committed baseline 5M tokens/min; effective observed ~3.5M tokens/min due to queueing and preemption effects.
- Error profile: 502s concentrated on long-tail requests (sequence lengths > 1024) from batch jobs + retries creating amplification.

Immediate impact vector: contention on KV cache + excessive concurrent long-sequence requests causing both per-core saturation and significantly higher scheduling latencies (redispatched work). The runtime’s preemption heuristics are causing fairness issues when long-running requests accumulate.

Prepared mitigations for the bridge:
1) Temporarily enable customer-specific burst pool (adds up to 2 GPU-equivalent burst capacity from our spare pool) — requires ops authorization and 30–60s warmup.
2) Selective routing: demote non-critical routes to a lower-cost model variant (quantized L2) for 60–120 minutes.
3) Apply per-route concurrency caps + prefer short-request slotting to avoid long-tail hogging.
4) Adjust preemption aggressiveness to favor short requests (risk: slightly higher p50 for long jobs).

I’ll bring live metrics on the bridge. If we choose 1) we will need a billing/exec nod for temporary burst usage and a decision on whether to convert to a short-term reserved uplift.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:05:45 -0800
Subject: Re: PivotalPay — Immediate headroom ceiling breach & reserved throughput shortfall

On Tue, Nov 2, 2027 at 09:37 AM marcus_lin@redwood.com wrote:
> Short RCA notes before the bridge:
> - Observation: Dedicated GPU pool nodes ...

Adding a technical mitigation plan (short-term + 24h):
Short-term (0–2h):
- Flip routing policy for PivotalPay write-heavy endpoints to model-small-v2 (8-bit quantized) for non-auth payment flows. Expected token cost: ~0.6x, p50 latency increase ~10–20ms, p99 reduction due to fewer preemptions.
- Enable per-customer KV prefix caching for repeated prefixes — reduces decoding cost on common prompts.
- Activate burst pool (2 GPU-equivalents). We’ll monitor queue depth; burst will be drained when traffic normalizes.

24-hour (stabilization):
- Schedule an autoscale window: increase reserved capacity by +1 GPU equivalent for 72 hours (billing discussion).
- Tune scheduler fairness: conservative change flagged as minor risk to long-seq latency but reduces 5xx rate.
- Run prompt-level evals to ensure quantized variant preserves acceptance criteria for your top-10 flows.

We will prepare a short canary test for the quantized model and push the routing change to 1 node first. Need approval to apply burst and to initiate the +1 GPU reserved commit for the next 72h.

— Karthik
Staff Engineer, Inference Performance

> Adding a technical mitigation plan (short-term + 24h):

Meera / PivotalPay execs — I’m Vivek (VP Product & Ops). Thanks for raising this. From Redwood’s side we’ll:
- Approve immediate activation of the 2-GPU burst runway for the next 4 hours to stabilize customer traffic.
- Support an expedited +1 GPU reserved uplift for 72 hours subject to a short commercial note (I’ll coordinate with finance).
- Offer a 48-hour service credit for any SLA misses tied directly to this event (we’ll finalize wording in the MOP).

Next steps I need from internal team:
1) Short-form mutual action plan (we’ll use the attached doc) and clear owner assignments.
2) A short communications note for PivotalPay customers (Priyom, please draft).
3) Post-incident follow-up: postmortem within 5 business days with concrete scheduler and capacity changes.

Meera — can we lock a 11:30 PST call with your CTO and our head of sales to confirm the uplift and communications cadence? If you prefer, we can convert the budget approval to an on-paper purchase order / short-term amendment.

— Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Product & Ops, Redwood Inference

2) Accountability — we want clear owners from Redwood for mitigation steps and a public-facing incident summary after stabilization.

We appreciate the offer of a 48-hour credit; please send the proposed wording during the bridge. Also please include a short, non-technical executive summary for our board (one page).
